conclusion: The five captured configuration files and the stated administrator trust assumptions can support a separately named single-GPU configured-isolation profile. They do not prove scheduler-to-physical mapping, kernel enforcement, active daemon identity or installed build equivalence.
implementation_requirements: Use an exact opt-in source capability and a complete versioned profile. Old/default plans, callers and consumers retain their current checks.

Introduce an explicit unresolved pre-submission physical-identity schema. Preserve null physical UUID and original scheduler/CUDA selectors; never bootstrap through logical-index/NVML-index/minor equality or a remembered GPU.

Write a separate immutable resolved binding tied to the exact source/configuration hashes, job/numeric step, ledger/submission/binding/release records and current PID/birth/all four UIDs. Do not modify the frozen plan.

Require fresh exact one-GPU typed logical job/step allocation and original matching job/step selectors, complete root-owned cgroup-v2 task membership, actual mount/namespace records and declared CPU/memory limits before GPU or numerical work.

Re-read exactly the five approved files and their exact include scope through unchanged ordinary descriptors and protected owner chains; require exact service identity, no group/other write permission and no competing cache/overrides. A changed baseline requires new review.

In the actual worker process keep CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES unchanged, require one CUDA-visible device and one JAX GPU, and join native CUDA UUID/PCI to one proc identity and Linux character-device major/minor. Never infer Linux minor from a Slurm index or CUDA compute-capability minor.

Select physical hardware metadata by the freshly observed UUID/PCI identity, not by numeric scheduler/NVML order. A host-wide NVML roster is inventory, not the allocated-device set. Retain model/memory/driver/runtime identity checks and immutable mapped-image capture.

If a parent sampler needs the physical UUID before worker timing, define the metadata-resolution/immutable-binding/ready sequence explicitly and preserve the full claimed capture interval. No guessed UUID or silent startup-peak omission; unsupported instrumented-capacity consumers must refuse.

Current, portable, final-training and capacity readers must each explicitly understand this profile and unresolved/resolved schema before accepting it. Unsupported paths fail closed; raw earlier failures cannot be relabelled.
Retain independent source/configuration/assets/software/precision and full numerical checks, then run separately reviewed zero-credit real producer fixtures before any formal or final admission.
required_negative_cases: Absent/implicit profile; Boolean or changed profile fields; foreign/missing/duplicated ledger or submission rows; wrong UID, PID/birth, numeric step or task membership.
Missing/changed file, service owner, passwd identity, include list, protected directory chain, writable path, alias, duplicate config, competing cache or unsupported GRES override.

Rewritten CUDA selector, stale resolved binding, guessed physical UUID, logical-index/minor equality requirement, ambiguous UUID/PCI/minor roster, mismatched CUDA/JAX device or changed mapped driver/backend bytes.
Unresolved plan accepted by an old reader, current/final/capacity worker admitted without its own explicit support, or metadata-only design/result granting admission.
More than one GPU/process/device or another host passed through the single-card profile.
scope_limit: One typed RTX A4500 on jaguar03, one owned numeric step and one worker process. No eight-card or other-host admission follows automatically.
controller_local_authority: The controller cgroup defaults and local cgroup.conf are separate observations; accepting the named local configuration is an explicit trust premise, not measured enforcement.

primary_source_checks.observation: The controller builds its configuration response with cgroup_get_conf_list.
Upstream initializes constraint defaults, reads cgroup.conf and packs configuration for stepd; this is not an attestation of the installed custom binary.
The versioned manual places cgroup.conf beside slurm.conf and describes daemon reload/restart application.
